propositions: The test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer test kills its xdist worker on macOS py3.13 due to exceeding the 300s per-test timeout budget when corpus iteration is load-dependent (91.6s idle, 504.8s saturated).
The test processes 884 renderable units serially in a single monolithic loop, performing ~1768 pandoc spawns, creating unbounded per-test cost that grows with corpus size and CPU contention.
pytest-timeout's thread method calls os._exit(1) from a timer thread, causing worker death without traceback or assertion text rather than a normal test failure.
The fix chunks the equivalence test into fixed-size batches (_EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK=40) via parametrization, bounding per-chunk cost to ~4s idle and enabling xdist parallelization across workers.

A new coverage guard test (test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit) verifies all 884 units remain compared by asserting chunk concatenation equals _renderable_units(), with _EQUIVALENCE_STRIDE still 1.
